title: Lewis Hamilton and Kimi Antonelli penalized after Hungarian GP qualifying
content:
Lewis Hamilton received a three-place grid penalty for the Hungarian Grand Prix for impeding Oscar Piastri on the McLaren driver’s last Q3 lap.

Hamilton, 41, initially qualified in second but will drop down to fifth for Sunday’s race start. After completing his flying Q3 lap, Hamilton was driving “at a significantly reduced speed on the racing line” when Piastri was starting a push lap, according to the stewards.

The Ferrari driver said in the post-race news conference that he was told Piastri was on a flying lap “literally when he was at the apex behind me, so I had no idea he was coming.” Hamilton told the stewards that due to where his car was positioned on Hungaroring, Piastri wasn’t “visible in his mirrors”.

Because the Briton was the first out, he was under the impression that the other drivers in Q3 had already completed their laps and that team-mate Charles Leclerc “was the car that was behind me when I left the pit lane.”

“Yeah,” Hamilton said. “Crazy, because it had been clean and obviously it wasn’t intentional.”

Piastri told Sky Sports after qualifying that “it was just Lewis not looking in his mirrors” and that “the yellow flag wasn’t my problem”. Between Hamilton’s impeding and the yellow flag triggered by Max Verstappen, the Australian couldn’t “get a lap in either way”, despite the car being quick.

Because Hamilton impeded him, Piastri had “to take avoiding action by running wide and being obliged to abort the lap.”

It comes on a weekend where McLaren brought a notable upgrade package, though pole sitter Lando Norris said, “It doesn’t feel that different. But it certainly seems to be going a little bit quicker, and that’s always a good thing.”

Norris managed to edge ahead of Hamilton by 0.012 seconds to take his first pole position of the season — and the first non-Mercedes pole position of 2026. The Silver Arrows, meanwhile, had a tricky day, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli initially qualifying fourth and George Russell down in seventh.

Russell needed to come to a stop at the end of Q3, rather than returning to the parc fermé area, due to a water leak, team boss Toto Wolff told Sky Sports. Mercedes later confirmed that it will change his engine, his fourth of the season (and within allocation), ahead of Sunday’s race.

Meanwhile, Antonelli found himself under investigation for an alleged yellow flag infringement, regarding his flying lap when Verstappen had a spin and triggered yellow flags. The stewards ultimately handed the Italian driver a three-place grid drop to seventh and a penalty point, his fourth penalty in a 12-month stretch.

According to the stewards’ decision document, Antonelli said he “lifted off the throttle earlier than his previous push lap”, when he saw the yellow flag and light panel. The telemetry may have confirmed that, but it was a short period where the Mercedes driver reduced his speed. Per the stewards, Antonelli’s speed when passing Verstappen’s incident “was slightly higher than that on the previous push lap.”

The decision document reads: “The mini sector time was only 0.03 second slower than his best time for that mini sector, and whilst, because he had lifted 16 metres earlier, he was 14 km/h slower entering the yellow flag sector, but was 3 km/h faster when passing the incident site due to less application of the brakes entering the corner.”

The standard penalty for this infraction is typically a five-place grid drop. The stewards took Antonelli slowing, though “an insufficient and unsustained,” into account, as well as him having “ limited time and distance to react”. That’s why it’s just a three-place grid drop.
